summary.oneLiner: Delta Corp faces near-term EBITDA pressure from a 6-7% GST cost shock on chip sales, but is counterbalancing it with doubling casino capacity via a new vessel and expanding into complementary hospitality and real estate to secure long-term growth beyond Goa's regulatory limits.

one-line thesis: Delta Corp faces near-term EBITDA pressure from a 6-7% GST cost shock on chip sales, but is counterbalancing it with doubling casino capacity via a new vessel and expanding into complementary hospitality and real estate to secure long-term growth beyond Goa's regulatory limits.
financial scorecard: rev: -12% YoY; EBITDA: -5-6% margin compression; PAT: -15% YoY; orderbook: N/A; netdebt: net cash position of ~₹500cr
guidance: Revenue to return to pre-GST levels by Q2FY25; EBITDA margins to stabilize at 35-36%; new vessel to contribute revenue from Q3FY24 onwards; online business to remain on hold pending industry shakeout.
segment / subsidiary detail: Casino: 124K visitations in Q3FY24 (-6% YoY); GGR per visitation stable; GST cost absorbed via promotional chips, resulting in 6% effective GGR reduction. Hospitality: ₹190cr spent on Miramar hotel; ₹175cr pending; 18-24mo timeline. Online: GST-induced marketing freeze; focus on poker only; industry consolidation expected. Real estate: ₹250cr earmarked for JV with Peninsula Land; focus on redevelopment in Mumbai/Goa; IRR target 25-30%.
growth verticals / optionality: New river vessel (2x capacity) to drive revenue growth from Q3FY24; integrated resort Phase I (water theme park) to launch in 18-24mo; real estate JV could unlock non-casino cash flows; potential upside from online industry consolidation.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin compressed from 41% to 35-36% due to 6-7% GST cost increase; fixed cost structure limits further margin erosion; variable costs down due to lower visitation but offset by higher legal costs.
capex / expansion: ₹280-290cr total for new vessel (₹175cr spent); ₹175cr pending for Miramar hotel; ₹250cr earmarked for Peninsula JV; ₹125-130cr in land for integrated resort (Phase I active); total FY24 capex ~₹600cr.
capital allocation: Prioritizing internal capex (vessel, hotel) over dividends; ₹500cr cash reserve intact; ₹250cr allocated to Peninsula JV for redevelopment projects; no debt planned; potential asset monetization (Advani stake) if opportune.
risks & watch-items: GST litigation risk (retrospective demands pending in High Court); regulatory freeze on casino licenses; tourism decline in Goa; online gaming profitability unsustainable; delays in vessel/hotel completion; real estate JV execution risk.
management quality / tone: Confident and proactive; acknowledges GST pain but emphasizes resilience of core business; clear roadmap for recovery via capacity expansion; transparent on challenges; optimistic on long-term growth via diversification.
non-obvious takeaways: The 70% GGR-to-chip-sales ratio reflects a structural behavioral shift: players now buy smaller chip amounts due to irreversible GST on deposits, reducing lifetime value per customer — a hidden revenue leak not captured in headline GGR.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Media, entertainment & out-of-home advertising
themes.need: Digital-content, music-IP licensing and an advertising-recovery cycle underpin media - TIPSMUSIC on music IP; ZEEL/ENIL/RADIOCITY/BTML on broadcast/content; HTMEDIA/DBCORP/HMVL on print + digital; SIGNPOST/BRIGHT-tier and UFO on OOH/cinema. Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
themes.driver: Festive ad-spend recovery; music-licensing/streaming monetization; OOH inventory uptake.
